provisions.title: Erasure on request
provisions.text: (3) A Data Principal shall make a request in such manner as may be prescribed to the Data Fiduciary for erasure of her personal data, and upon receipt of such a request, the Data Fiduciary shall erase her personal data unless retention of the same is necessary for the specified purpose or for compliance with any law for the time being in force.

provisions.title: Erasure of personal data
provisions.text: (7) A Data Fiduciary shall, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law for the time being in force,— (a) erase personal data, upon the Data Principal withdrawing her consent or as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the specified purpose is no longer being served, whichever is earlier; and … (b) cause its Data Processor to erase any personal data that was made available by the Data Fiduciary for processing to such Data Processor.

provisions.title: Erasure by Data Processor
provisions.text: (b) cause its Data Processor to erase any personal data that was made available by the Data Fiduciary for processing to such Data Processor.

provisions.title: Right to correction and erasure of personal data
provisions.text: (1) A Data Principal shall have the right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of her personal data for the processing of which she has previously given consent, including consent as referred to in clause (a) of section 7, in accordance with any requirement or procedure under any law for the time being in force.

provisions.title: General obligations of Data Fiduciary
provisions.text: (1) A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or failure of a Data Principal to carry out the duties provided under this Act, be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
provisions.text: The product generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.

value.reason: The POST /dataerasure handler in routes/dataErasure.ts (lines 74-132) checks that the user is logged in, then only calls PrivacyRequestModel.create({ UserId: loggedInUser.data.id, deletionRequested: true }). This records that the user asked for deletion. It does not erase anything. In the code shown, nothing calls UserModel.destroy, anonymizes the user, or removes the email address from the Users table. The data flow shows the email is collected at registration (register.component.html, then POST /api/Users), stored in models/user.ts, and later returned in responses (routes/changePassword.ts, routes/saveLoginIp.ts), so it stays in the system after the request. This matches the positive RET-02 example, which only logs a deletion request, and differs from the negative example, which also calls User.destroy. Section 12(3) requires the Data Fiduciary to erase the data once it receives the request, unless the law or the specified purpose requires keeping it. The code gives no such reason and has no retention logic. Caveat: the handler excerpt is cut off after the create call. If a later part of lines 74-132 deletes or anonymizes the data, this would be a false positive. In the standard version of this handler (OWASP Juice Shop), the rest only clears the session cookie and renders a confirmation page.
